title: Through the pointer
description:
Write two functions that work through a pointer, and are careful about `nullptr`:

- `void setToZero(int* p)` sets the pointed-to `int` to 0. If `p` is null it does nothing.
- `int valueOr(const int* p, int fallback)` returns the pointed-to value, or `fallback` if `p` is null.

`*p` follows the pointer to the value it points at. Following a null pointer crashes the program, so always check first.
